name: Oswald Mosley
role: British MP and leader of the British Union of Fascists (1932–1940) and Union Movement (post-war)
summary: Mosley moved from Conservative to Independent to Labour MP, proposed an expansionist unemployment programme in 1930, and then led the New Party, the British Union of Fascists (a corporatist, authoritarian, protectionist and antisemitic programme) and, after wartime internment, the Union Movement. His mature position, 'Europe a Nation', combined a single elected European government and a planned wage-price economy with racial separation and opposition to immigration and communism.

sources.title: The Alternative (1947)
sources.author: Oswald Mosley
sources.usedFor: Post-war statement of his new thinking: European union, government by an executive subject to dismissal by direct vote, industrial organisations, race and function, Jewish national home, Soviet communism, God and progress. Full text read.

sources.title: My Life (1968)
sources.author: Oswald Mosley
sources.usedFor: Autobiography including the Union Movement, the 1962 Venice European Declaration (quoted in full), the 1959 North Kensington campaign, apartheid and Africa, and his Holocaust remarks.

sources.title: Fascism: 100 Questions Asked and Answered (1936)
sources.author: Oswald Mosley
sources.usedFor: British Union of Fascists programme in his own words: Corporate State, economy, wages, tariffs, women, Jews, Empire. Pre-war position, used only where he later repeated or did not revise it.

sources.title: The Greater Britain (1932)
sources.author: Oswald Mosley
sources.usedFor: Founding BUF programme: state and citizen, private liberty, women, India and the Empire.

sources.title: Hansard, Commons, 28 May 1930 (Privy Seal Office debate), Sir Oswald Mosley's speech
sources.author: Oswald Mosley (as reported in Hansard)
sources.usedFor: His Commons speech on unemployment: machinery of government, import control, home market, pensions and public works.

sources.title: Oswald Mosley
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Biographical background and secondary reports of his Union Movement, 1959 campaign, Holocaust remarks and 1968 letter to The Times.

universal-healthcare.rationale: In 1936 he kept voluntary hospitals but promised state funding, a national director of hospitals and hospital accommodation for every citizen who needs it. Not a fully state-provided system, and pre-war only.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Pre-war the corporations were to raise wages systematically and prohibit wage-cutting; the 1962 Venice declaration he drafted called for equal wages across Europe rising as productivity rises. No statutory minimum wage as such.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Rejected laissez-faire as the chaos in which finance rules; private enterprise was to be free only within boundaries set by a directing state and a national plan.

public-ownership.rationale: In The Alternative he called nationalisation the purchase of obsolete industries at public expense and wanted the state to create new enterprise instead; in the 1962 Venice declaration he said nationalised industries would be better under workers' ownership or syndicalism than state bureaucracy.

unions-good.rationale: In 1936 he said unions would be a main pillar of the Corporate State and keep their benefits, but wanted them removed from party politics and criticised their leaders' block vote.

property-fundamental.rationale: Held that land and hereditary wealth are a trusteeship: an abusing landlord loses land without compensation and hereditary wealth reverts to the state unless service is given.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Private enterprise could 'serve but not exploit'; the state was to set limits by law, control banking, and intervene against monopoly (1936, 1947, 1962).

cut-welfare.rationale: Favoured pensions at 60 and an end to the Means Test, though he also wanted the unemployed to be offered real work at decent wages 'or you get nothing'.

worker-ownership.rationale: Stated in 1962 that already-nationalised industries would be better run by workers' ownership or syndicalism, and that ownership would become irrelevant under his wage-price mechanism. Not a general demand.

strong-leader.rationale: Argued for an executive with 'absolute power of action', subject only to dismissal by direct popular vote, and for the leadership principle (1936, 1947).

state-harmful.rationale: Wanted a 'Creative and Directive State' with executive power; the state is to create and construct, not wither.

empower-police-military.rationale: In 1936 he wanted Britain rearmed, with an air force equal to any and a modernised army and fleet; no statement found on police powers.

decide-locally.rationale: Points both ways: in 1936 national policy had to prevail over local authorities, yet he also wanted Welsh and Scottish matters settled 'on the spot' and local questions decided by the man on the spot.

traditional-family.rationale: Honoured motherhood as one of the highest callings; wanted a family wage so wives need not go out to work, with a corporation to represent mothers.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Valued national pride and tradition and the 'unique culture' of Europe; in 1962 declared the splendour of European history and traditions must never be surrendered.

gradual-change.rationale: Demanded a 'revolution in the machinery of government' (Hansard, 1930) and a dynamic transition to a new civilisation, rejecting the static and the gradual.

reduce-immigration.rationale: In 1936 said all immigration would be stopped; in 1959 he stood on ending coloured immigration and repatriating recent immigrants with fares paid.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Rejected the League and the UN as artificial internationalism; his 1962 declaration said Europe as a third power would end the political and military power of the UN.

free-trade.rationale: Called laissez-faire and free trade irrelevant to the modern world; advocated import control, exclusion of cheap foreign goods and an insulated bloc.

nation-first.rationale: Mixed: pre-war 'Britain first' and rejection of internationalism, but from 1946 he urged extending patriotism to Europe as one nation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: In 1958 he wrote that a united Europe should prevent massacre of a million and a half Jews or any comparable community if within its power. He did not specify military force.

open-borders.rationale: Wanted immigration ended; his 1962 declaration gave non-Europeans in Europe no vote or political rights. A single Europe was to have a common government, but not an open world.

limit-growth.rationale: Wanted production to expand continually so wages and living standards could rise with science; no environmental argument for limits.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Held that poverty could have been solved long ago by efficient government and that modern science makes a new civilisation possible; politics must harness it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Said power would be sought by legal and constitutional means, and pledged against imprisonment without trial; yet he spoke of a Fascist revolution and a revolution in government machinery.

experts-over-public.rationale: Argued that subjects should be discussed only by those who understand them, that the public can only judge results, and that Parliament should be elected on an occupational basis.

central-planning.rationale: Described the Corporate State as a planned economy and wanted a national plan to which industry conforms, while leaving private enterprise to run daily business.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Hereditary wealth was not to be permitted without service; what service did not justify would revert to the state (1936).

basic-income.rationale: Rejected the Douglas Social Credit national dividend paid to rich and poor irrespective of service.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Told the Commons in 1930 for import control boards and a protected home market, and later for an insulated European bloc.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Wanted credit and capital directed to national purposes, a ban on capital export, and in 1962 capital for underdeveloped regions of Europe.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Wanted land in as many hands as possible, owner-occupier farms, co-operatives and small shopkeepers, and 'capital in as many hands as possible'; opposed both state ownership and concentration in a few hands.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: His system rested on raising wages and a wage-price mechanism, not on abolishing wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Wanted the money supply to be a prerogative of the Crown, with a state-controlled banking corporation, not left to the market.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Advocated corporations of employers and workers with equal representation setting wages and conditions within national limits; in 1947 he said these industrial organisations were still relevant.

one-party-rule.rationale: Pre-war he wanted to end the party system; his 1962 European declaration provided for elections which all parties may enter.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Pledged absolute loyalty to the Crown and wanted the sovereign to choose a new government after a lost vote (1936, 1947).

democracy-best.rationale: Dismissed existing 'democracy' as charlatanism and bureaucratic rule, while keeping direct popular votes on governments and, in 1962, free European elections.

direct-votes.rationale: Held that citizens should not decide matters they do not understand; they should only vote yes or no on a government's results.

right-to-secede.rationale: Opposed splitting up Great Britain into 'primitive anarchy'.

natural-rulers.rationale: Held that men differ in capacity, that the leader is selected by nature through ability to attract a following, and that statesmen should be trained for politics.

political-violence-never.rationale: Said Blackshirts 'shall certainly meet force with force' against opponents' violence, and that he was ready for the 'politics of passion' if forced.

separate-church-state.rationale: Quoted 'render unto Caesar the things that are Caesar's' as the Fascist attitude to religion and promised complete toleration. He still wanted religion represented in the second chamber.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Rejected religious creeds claiming to be the word of God, and drew his idea of divine purpose from nature and evidence rather than scripture.

military-superiority.rationale: Wanted Britain's air force equal to any and, in 1962, a Europe as strongly armed as America or Russia.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Valued the 'British race' kept without mixture, and in 1947 and 1962 a European race with a common ancestry and 'communion of blood'.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Called class war barbarous and rejected Marxian determinism; the Corporate State was to replace class struggle with cooperation.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Insisted that men differ in function and capacity and that reward follows service; only function differences, not class, were to remain.

civilizational-union.rationale: Called for Europe a Nation, uniting a continent with a shared three-thousand-year civilisation, and extending patriotism to kindred peoples including Americans.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Preached service: 'no reward without service' and obligation in public life.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Fascist principle was 'liberty in private life, obligation in public life'; the majority's right to act outweighs a minority's objection.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Celebrated modern science and wanted a union of European tradition with it.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Said science compelled a commensurate change in political thinking and that evolution must be deliberately accelerated; 'we must make new men'.

restore-past-order.rationale: Contrasted the static with the 'Becoming' and wanted continuous progress to higher forms, not a return.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Held that governments should be judged by results and that economic solutions are many, with the will to act what matters; in 1962 he said ownership becomes irrelevant under his wage-price mechanism.

direct-action.rationale: Said power would be won by legal and constitutional means through a parliamentary majority.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred: from his insistence on progress through science to ever higher forms of life.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Argued that function and differentiation follow from natural differences, and defended it against equalitarian doctrine.

distribute-by-need.rationale: 'Reward by result' and 'no reward without service' were his principles.

production-for-use.rationale: Accepted private profit within national limits: private enterprise could be 'free both in enterprise and profit' while it serves.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Held that excessive profit and unlimited finance exploit, but rejected the Marxist theory and kept profit within limits.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Condemned Soviet communism as despotism of a small clique.

collective-farming.rationale: Wanted as many owner-occupier farmers as possible, with land handed from father to son.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: In 1936 he said the struggle for markets is the main cause of war, but he blamed international finance and internationalism, not capitalism as such.

taxation-theft.rationale: Inferred: his programmes relied on budgetary expenditure and state loans, e.g. 1930 pension and public works schemes.

harm-principle.rationale: 1932 test: an action that does not harm the state or other citizens and leaves the doer sound in mind and body cannot be morally wrong; he also wanted citizens to 'live like athletes'.

positive-liberty.rationale: Said real freedom is economic freedom: good wages, short hours, opportunity for leisure; a vote means nothing otherwise.

organic-representation.rationale: Proposed an occupational franchise with corporations for each industry and one for mothers instead of geographical party politics.

total-state.rationale: Said the Fascist state asks service in public life but leaves private life free; he also criticised totalitarian bureaucracy.

national-rebirth.rationale: Presented Fascism as the national revival that ends decadence of the old parties.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Approved Japanese expansion into north China in 1936 and in 1962 claimed for a united Europe a third of Africa; but in 1936 he said Britons fight only to defend the Empire.

universal-morality.rationale: Described a 'supreme moral law' that forbids killing helpless prisoners, but also stressed natural differences between races.

single-common-good.rationale: Wanted the party game ended and discussion to be a mutual search for truth rather than debate between interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In 1947 he proposed partition of Palestine, giving the Jews a national home, with additional living space elsewhere.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Wanted industrial organisations in which employers and workers jointly run their own trades and give constant advice to government.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Urged public works and credit expansion, including state-guaranteed loans, against Treasury orthodoxy.

economic-freedom.rationale: Held that political liberty without economic security is hollow, but he meant security and wages rather than market liberty.

national-self-determination.rationale: In 1962 declared colonialism ended and Africa partly under African governments; he condemned domination of one people by another and wanted a Jewish national home.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Said the proper test of the unemployed is a good job at good wages: 'take it and do it, or you get nothing'.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Corporate State was to replace class war with representation of employers and workers together.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Wanted to combine the undying tradition of Europe with modern science and said Europe's history must never be surrendered.

workers-nation.rationale: Described his socialism as national, in contradistinction to international socialism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: 'We want men who are men and women who are women'; motherhood to be honoured and represented; but women could work and get equal pay.

ban-interest.rationale: Wanted a producer and consumer system free of usury; he did not propose an outright legal ban on interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: From 1948 he proposed dividing Africa between black and white states and called for 'genuine apartheid', but rejected ghetto-style segregation within white territory.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Said government is run for vested interests and finance, but rejected Marxist theory of the state.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Called party politicians 'racketeers' and 'old gang', and said democracy is ruled by vested interests.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: In 1936 said the unfit would be offered segregation or voluntary sterilisation, 'none will be sterilised against their will'.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Wanted a creative state directing national life, not a limited state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: In 1936 said education should teach the British what racial mixtures are bad, and law if needed; in 1947 spoke of holding the breed line; in 1959 favoured a ban on mixed marriages.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Allowed that all may be equal in the sight of God but called equality before the law humbug and denied equal capacity between races.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Held the people's will, expressed by direct vote, must decide whether governments continue; the 1962 declaration called for free elections of European government.

trade-surplus.rationale: Told the Commons that Britain need not export enough to build a favourable balance for foreign investment; foreign investment would be ended.

population-transfer.rationale: In 1936 he said Jews who did not put Britain first would be deported; in 1959 he proposed repatriating recent coloured immigrants with fares paid.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Described progress as driven by challenge and by the survival of the fittest, though he wanted peaceful union rather than strife between peoples.

separated-powers.rationale: Insisted that 'authority must never be divided' and that the executive must be supreme.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes and lockouts were to end as class war instruments under the Corporate State (1936).

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Argued that union of unlike peoples produces maximum friction and that a sudden influx with a different way of life harms social peace.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Denounced Regulation 18B detention without trial and pledged never to join a government that imprisons without trial.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Wanted government power to control prices and prevent speculators' exploitation; 1962 included intervention at prices where monopoly prevails.

party-controls-media.rationale: Wanted the press to print the truth and the state to be able to sue newspapers, but he did not call for government or party control.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: His 1962 declaration set up a common European government for foreign policy, defence, economic policy and finance, elected by all Europe.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Wanted the Crown's prerogative of choosing ministers restored; the Crown was to select new government after dismissal.

clerical-rule.rationale: Said religion and the state have different spheres and that executive must be supreme.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Opposed Puritan repression and D.O.R.A.-style legislation, preferring social sense to law.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: A government would stand or fall only on direct popular votes at intervals, with no limit on its tenure.

recall-officials.rationale: Governments could be dismissed by censure or direct vote and Corporation representatives by periodic vote.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Said Germans' overriding desire for reunion should be met within a united Europe.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Wrote that it is useless to argue all races are equally gifted and contrasted European achievement with that of other races.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Accepted evolution, indeed built his idea of purpose on it, and ridiculed creeds claiming to be the word of God.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred: from his statement that Jews would be treated as foreigners and denied full citizenship, and that naturalised foreigners would be deported.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Argued executive power was needed in a period of transition, with the law changed openly; majority consent was required.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: His 1962 plan confined nuclear weapons to three great powers, including a united Europe, until mutual disarmament.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Kept the Crown as head of state.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Told the Commons banking should not displace government control and wanted the money supply under the Crown.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property is trusteeship; private enterprise may serve but not exploit.

collective-defense.rationale: Wanted Britain and Europe united with the West in collective security against Soviet Russia and, in 1962, European solidarity.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Looked to the Crown as the dispassionate instrument selecting an alternative government.

character-from-environment.rationale: Held men are born with varying gifts and capacities, and drew breeding analogies for human stock.

land-redistribution.rationale: Absentee or abusing landlords would lose land without compensation and it would be split into owner-occupier farms.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred: his 1962 declaration put finance and economic policy under one European government.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Argued for extending patriotism to all of like kind, the idea of kinship.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Held that Jews should be given a national home and cannot claim dual nationality.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Called Marxian determinism absurd and stressed the will to action.

ban-cartels.rationale: Wanted chain stores and monopolies broken up and state action where monopoly conditions prevail, though his own corporations organised industries.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Held that the right of the majority is greater than that of the minority and that a majority may change the law.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Called for a self-contained National and Empire economic system independent of foreign markets, and in 1947 for a European-African bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Wanted equal wage conditions across a common market to avoid wage competition; no environmental standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: Wanted rewards by results and higher wages as production grows.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Wanted the House of Lords abolished and hereditary wealth tied to service, but kept the Crown.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Defended British rule in India as a duty and in 1947 wanted Europeans to develop Africa, but in 1962 called for an end to colonialism.

public-money-creation.rationale: Wanted currency issue to be the Crown's prerogative rather than a private monopoly.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Predicted a new economic crisis; he thought capitalism would only avoid collapse by distributing surplus.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Held majorities may change the law and that minority rights must not block national action.

minority-veto.rationale: Rejected letting one man's conscientious objection forbid a nation to save itself.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Wanted Parliament as technical adviser while the executive acts, with power to dismiss resting with the people.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Landowners were to be regarded as trustees giving local leadership and service in return for reward.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Wanted a dedicated life of service, not the withdrawal of a monk.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Said the national press is a 'dope machine' of vested interests, and that people are made drunk with the wine of flattery.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Described the people being flattered into believing they control a system run by vested interests.

native-born-offices.rationale: Said anyone in state service under Fascism must be entirely British, with foreigners barred from being MPs or officials.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Called it folly to claim fascism and communism are identical and distinguished them sharply.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Held that fascism takes a different national form in each nation and that multi-racial government breaks down in Africa.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Wanted private tenure of land widely diffused and passed from father to son.

corporate-influence.rationale: Said government is under vested interest, finance and monopoly.

job-guarantee.rationale: Wanted the government to organise public works so the unemployed are offered a good job at good wages.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred: his corporations were organised by industry rather than craft.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Said Jews had organised as a nation within the nation putting their interests first, and that Finance Houses 'largely Jewish' could break governments; by 1947 he framed it as a national-home question.

informal-organisation.rationale: Built a disciplined hierarchical movement on the leadership principle.

religious-nation.rationale: Promised complete religious toleration; he defined nation by race and culture.

defeat-communism.rationale: Urged in 1947 that America compel Russia to accept inspection by ultimatum if necessary and described Soviet communism as a menace to Western civilisation.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Kept voluntary hospitals with state funding and coordination.

religion-illusion.rationale: Argued God exists from evidence of design and called the Soviet denial of spiritual creeds a menace.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred: his family policy kept mothers in the home with a family wage.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: 1962 declaration described a third system, producer state, superior to American capitalism and communist bureaucracy.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Claimed Europeans' place in southern Africa on history, citing arrival in 1652 before the black tribes.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Mixed: in 1968 he condemned the killing of Jews as a hideous crime but said the figures were disputed; in 1947 he called camp conditions partly a result of Allied bombing.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Condemned Regulation 18B and in 1962 provided for elections open to all parties.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Said development of Africa would supply raw materials to British industry and the 1936 Empire programme served the home market; he later called for an end to colonialism.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Wanted people to take part in decisions in their own trades through industrial organisations.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Said he was never a man of the right and sought a synthesis reconciling authority with liberty.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Held that a government's authority rests on the people's direct vote; he saw God's purpose in nature, not in any source of political authority.

social-market-economy.rationale: Wanted private enterprise inside national boundaries with fair competition conditions (1947, 1962).

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Rejected disarmament by Britain alone and insisted on a strong, armed Europe.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: 1962: Europe a third power outside both American and Russian blocs.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Said press freedom means the right of millionaires to corner newspapers.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: In 1947 said laws should be open and not retrospective, but earlier planned government by Order.

racial-franchise.rationale: 1962 declaration: Europeans in non-European territory and non-Europeans in European territory would have no vote or political rights.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Said finance and monopoly make government a captive of vested interest.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Argued Union of Europe is a first condition of human survival given atomic weapons.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: 1962: non-Europeans in Europe without vote or political rights.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: His 1962 declaration called for immediate withdrawal of Russian and American forces and bases from Europe.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Held no reward without service; hereditary wealth must be justified by service.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: he accepted meeting force with force.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Spoke of a European breed and culture on a hundred generations and Roman stock remaining in Britain.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Presented fascism's successor idea against communism as a spiritual conflict.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Said chain stores owned by Jewish and foreign capital would be eliminated and denied alien control of vital supplies.

independent-unions.rationale: Wanted unions inside the Corporate State and removed from political control.

second-chamber.rationale: Would replace the House of Lords with a Senate of industry, culture and ability.

family-wage.rationale: Wage to be enough that the man can maintain the home.

person-over-state.rationale: Held every man gives his public life to the state in return for private liberty.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Called for politics serving higher forms of life, values of the spirit, and believed in God.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Wanted delegated powers for Wales and Scotland but with overall national unity.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Argued for British racial pride and a European 'communion of blood'.

racial-pride.rationale: Credited the British social sense and pride of race.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: In 1936 said Britons fight only to defend the Empire.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred: he wanted Europe as one nation across languages.

free-public-college.rationale: Wanted all to have equal opportunity of education and specialised training through university for those of talent.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Valued mothers' counsel and representation in the state.

arms-reduction.rationale: Willing to disarm if others do and security is not impaired.

capital-controls.rationale: Export of credit or capital to be absolutely prohibited.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Wages set within corporations with employers and workers represented.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: advocated credit expansion and loan-financed schemes.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Argued for a single planned corporate system.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Wanted to make new men and accelerate human evolution.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Said the tenets of different creeds cannot all be right.

farm-price-support.rationale: Assured prices and import exclusion for farmers; told the Commons for wheat import control.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: 1962: Europe must be as strongly armed as America or Russia until mutual disarmament.

women-suffrage.rationale: Women eligible on all corporations and full participation, equal pay.

race-social-construct.rationale: Insisted differences between races are observable fact.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Condemned Nuremberg as retrospective law and a peace of vengeance.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Called creeds claimed as the word of God a priori and mutually incompatible.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Favoured wide delegated powers to Welsh and Scottish on local questions.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred: from his pledge against imprisonment without trial.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Pledged in 1962 to be true to fellow Europeans threatened in Africa.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Opposed the Means Test and supported pensions at 60.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: 'Nothing shall come between Government and People'; ended the party game.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: 1946: union of Europe's undying tradition and modern science.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Wanted wages rising and hours shortening as science increases production.

notes: Views changed after 1945: pre-war he sought a one-nation corporate state under the British Union of Fascists, with party politics abolished and Jews to be deported or denied citizenship; from 1946-1948 he called for a union of Europe, and the 1962 Venice declaration provided for free elections open to all parties. Where the post-war texts (The Alternative, My Life) state a position they were used; where they are silent but he said his earlier economic and governmental proposals remained relevant (The Alternative, preface and chapter V), the 1936 programme is used, usually at medium or low confidence. His own words on the Holocaust (1968) accept mass killing as a crime but treat the scale as open; secondary reports (Wikipedia) describe further denialist claims, hence 0 at low confidence. Archive.org texts are OCR and were read through search and targeted reading, not every page.
